title: install-config.json
description: Written by the Bootsahi macOS app onto the ESP (<ESP>/bootsahi/install-config.json) after the user completes the wizard. Consumed once, at first boot, by bootsahi-agent, which never re-reads it after a successful install.

targetImgref.description: OCI ref to deploy, e.g. ghcr.io/tuna-os/bonito:gnome-asahi. Must resolve to an arm64 bootc image.

rootPartition.description: Block device for the root filesystem (e.g. /dev/nvme0n1p5). PROVISIONAL: per docs/UNIFIED-INSTALL-CONTRACT.md this field is slated to become a dev/test override rather than an app-supplied input. The macOS app cannot produce a correct value even in principle -- it knows the partition as 'disk0s5', while the agent sees 'nvme0n1p5' -- so the agent should resolve the target at runtime from a PARTUUID recorded by the backend. Still required today because how it resolves depends on an unsettled partition-layout decision (see that doc's 'fisherman formats /' section).

espPartition.description: Block device for the EFI system partition shared with recoveryOS/m1n1 (e.g. /dev/nvme0n1p1). Same PROVISIONAL status as rootPartition. Note the agent always emits this mount with fstype 'unformatted': the ESP already holds m1n1/boot.bin and the non-redistributable on-device-extracted vendorfw/, so it must never be reformatted.

filesystem.description: Filesystem to format rootPartition with. zfs is not offered here (fisherman's zfs path assumes whole-disk auto-partitioning, not a pre-made partition).

encryption.description: LUKS passphrases are asked for on the machine at first boot, never stored here. A config containing encryption.passphrase is refused (issue #21).

password.description: MUST be a crypt hash (e.g. $6$ SHA-512), never the password as typed. This file is written to an unencrypted, world-readable FAT ESP and is deliberately retained after a failed install so the UI can retry, so a reusable credential must never appear here (issue #21). bootsahi-agent refuses a config whose password is not $-prefixed; fisherman applies such a value verbatim via chpasswd -e.

wifi.description: SSID only. The passphrase is NEVER written here: this file lives on an unencrypted, world-readable FAT ESP that is deliberately retained after a failed install, and encrypting it would not help because any key the agent could use unattended must sit on the same disk an attacker already has. bootsahi-agent asks for the Wi-Fi password at first boot via systemd-ask-password and REFUSES a config containing wifi.psk (issue #21).

sshEnabled.description: Enables sshd in the bootstrap for the headless/M1-Air-test-loop path (D1).

cosignIdentity.description: REQUIRED. Expected cosign certificate identity for targetImgref. bootsahi-agent verifies the image signature before deploying and refuses to install if this is absent -- an omittable policy is not a policy, and this file lives on a world-readable vfat ESP (issue #24). The agent deploys the digest cosign reports, not the tag, so the bytes verified are the bytes installed.

cosignIssuer.description: REQUIRED, and paired with cosignIdentity. An identity without a pinned issuer would be accepted from ANY OIDC provider, so a half-policy is refused exactly like a missing one.
